items.cite: Adrienne Fried Block, *Amy Beach, Passionate Victorian: The Life and Work of an American Composer, 1867–1944* (Oxford University Press, 1998).
items.note: The standard life, covering how a prodigy with one year of formal harmony came to compose a symphony. It is the source of the Amy Beach Project’s works list.

items.cite: Walter S. Jenkins, *The Remarkable Mrs. Beach, American Composer* (Harmonie Park Press, 1994).
items.note: A life drawn from her scrapbooks and letters, now at the University of New Hampshire, covering the marriage, the Cape Cod cottage and the MacDowell summers.

items.cite: Jeanell Wise Brown, *Amy Beach and Her Chamber Music* (Scarecrow Press, 1994).
items.note: A study of the chamber music, including the Violin Sonata, the Piano Quintet and the late trio.

items.cite: Boston Symphony Orchestra, programme book for the third rehearsal and concert, 30–31 October 1896 (Season 16, subscription series).
items.note: The programme that listeners read at the first performance of the “Gaelic” Symphony gives Beach’s training, the movements, the scoring and the Celtic cadence.

items.cite: Library of Congress Music Division, *Amy Beach: A Guide to Primary and Secondary Resources at the Library of Congress* (research guide).
items.note: The locations of the manuscripts and first editions are given here. The Schmidt archive, her letters to the Library and the published scores are listed.
